aggregated_directions.explanation: This neuron is acting like a “word‐ending” detector for multi-character or multi-syllable content words (especially in CJK text, but also in code names, list indices, Korean or English compounds).  It lights up on the final token of a semantically meaningful unit—e.g. the last character of a Chinese/Japanese noun (“会” in “大会,” “阵” in “矩阵,” “章” in “文章,” “答” in “回答,” etc.), the closing syllable of a Korean word (“레스” in “스트레스”), the end of a tab-label (“卡” in “选项卡2”), or the final element of a code identifier (“constant” in `tf.constant`), list number (“3.” in bullet lists), and so on.  In short, it marks the completion of a discrete lexical chunk.

In short, it marks the completion of a discrete lexical chunk.
